title: Normalized coefficient evaluation of cartesian open base change
statement: Let R_n be any sequence of commutative rings with ring-homomorphism transitions. Let r:V->S, k:V->W, i:S->T, p:W->T be a cartesian square ri=kp with k and i open immersions. Use the normalized pullback and open evaluation isomorphisms of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], and openBaseChange of [def-sp-varying-ring-clopen-arrow-factors]. Fix n. There exists a natural transformation a from D(i_!) D(p^*) to D(r^*) D(k_!) between the actual single-coefficient R_n module-derived categories such that the evaluated openBaseChange is a after these four comparisons. Explicitly for every N in D(system_S), ev_W(openBaseChange_N);evalJ_k(G_r N);J_k(evalG_r(N)) = evalG_p(J_i N);G_p(evalJ_i(N));a(ev_S N). The same a satisfies the identical equation for StrictTower.beta at every input of D(strict towers over R_n), using strict evaluation at zero and its specified evalG and evalJ. There is no finiteness, properness or quasi-compactness assumption.

Apply mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_comp of [lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition] at the natural-isomorphism level to obtain the derived normalized pullback-composition equation. proof.text: Define the single-coefficient inverse beta to be the open-adjunction mate of the inverse exact-localized single-coefficient square. Exact localization preserves the specified ordinary unit equation defining moduleBetaInv, so the varying inverse beta has that same square as its mate. Open evaluation is the inverse mate of evalG by definition. Apply the horizontal/vertical mate interchange law and the pullback-square evaluation equation to obtain the inverse-beta comparison. For strict towers, evalD_square gives the pullback-square equation termwise, and exact_mate applied to the ordinary whiskered open adjunction proves that strict evalJ inverse is the corresponding open mate. The same mate interchange proves the strict inverse-beta comparison, with exactly the same single-coefficient inverse beta.

proof.text: For a cartesian open square StrictTower.betaInv is invertible for arbitrary coefficient rings. In its just-proved coefficient equation the other four comparison factors are invertible, so the single-coefficient inverse beta is invertible on every evaluated strict derived tower. Every single-coefficient derived object is isomorphic to the evaluation of its constant derived tower, by constantEval. Naturality along this isomorphism transfers invertibility to every object, without assuming faithfulness of evaluation. Thus the single-coefficient inverse beta is an invertible natural transformation. Take its actual inverse for a. Multiplying each inverse-beta equation by its six invertible comparison factors gives the two displayed forward equations. This is a complete Lean proof, with no new geometric or localization holes.

lean.statement:
theorem openBaseChangeEvaluation {V W S T : Scheme.{u}} (k : V ⟶ W) (r : V ⟶ S)
    (p : W ⟶ T) (i : S ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i]
    (h : r ≫ i = k ≫ p) (hsq : IsPullback r k i p) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ a : (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) i).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          (StrictTower.modulePullback (R n) p).mapDerivedCategory ⟶
        (StrictTower.modulePullback (R n) r).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) k).mapDerivedCategory,
      (∀ N : Derived R φ S,
        (ev R φ W n).map ((openBaseChange R φ r k i p h hsq).app N) ≫
            (evalJ R φ k n).hom.app ((G R φ r).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) k).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((evalG R φ r n).hom.app N) =
          (evalG R φ p n).hom.app ((J R φ i).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.modulePullback (R n) p).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((evalJ R φ i n).hom.app N) ≫ a.app ((ev R φ S n).obj N)) ∧
      (∀ N : StrictTower.Derived (R n) S,
        (StrictTower.ev (R n) W 0).map ((StrictTower.beta (R n) r k i p h hsq).hom.app N) ≫
            (StrictTower.evalJ (R n) k 0).hom.app ((StrictTower.G (R n) r).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) k).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((StrictTower.evalG (R n) r 0).hom.app N) =
          (StrictTower.evalG (R n) p 0).hom.app ((StrictTower.J (R n) i).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.modulePullback (R n) p).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((StrictTower.evalJ (R n) i 0).hom.app N) ≫
            a.app ((StrictTower.ev (R n) S 0).obj N))
